result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers see the tour as a list of interface parts rather than a task, and both cut the sidebar, top bar and dashboard steps by name. B goes further by having the user actually complete a first invoice, with a pre-filled sample and a confirmation message, and its Assumptions section suggests checking whether skippers create invoices later. A has a useful checklist and activation metrics, but it states its causes with more certainty, and it wrongly says users click Next nine times when the tour has six Next clicks. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly see the tour as a passive list of interface parts, and both name which steps to cut or defer. A is better because it makes the person actually create a sample invoice as a guided first task, and its check (do step-1 skippers create an invoice later?) speaks directly to the step-1 skip rate. B offers a good checklist and tips shown when needed, but it states its causes with more certainty than the data supports ("means the pitch failed", "nobody needs them explained"), and its flow leans on an empty-state button rather than guiding the person through doing the task.
